subject: Service provider onboarding & interstate transfer playbook - HealthSys
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@healthsys.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@healthsys.com>, Mike Walsh <mike.walsh@healthsys.com>
Date: 2025-09-16T14:14:00-07:00
Subject: Initial RFI - CPRA/service provider designation + dataflow questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our procurement review for the pilot, Legal/Security have a handful of clarifying questions before we can move to the DPA redline stage:

1) We need explicit language that Redwood will act as a "service provider" under CPRA/California law. Can you confirm that designation and provide any suggested language for the DPA?

2) Telemetry and usage logs: does Redwood consider telemetry used for service improvement to be "recipient-limited" (i.e., not subject to sale) and bounded to the service provider purpose? We need a short description of the telemetry types and retention windows.

3) Subprocessors: please provide your current list and your notice window for additions. If you have an onshore fallback / emergency subprocessors playbook (for on-prem fallback or data locality), that would be helpful.

4) Interstate transfers: HealthSys must understand where customer data may transit. Can you provide a transfer-map showing regions/third-party hops?

We're attaching our procurement worksheet (attached). If you can send a redline DPA that incorporates the SP designation and any limits on telemetry we can review. Would appreciate a call this week if possible.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Senior Contracts Manager | HealthSys Procurement
Elena.Park@healthsys.com

Attachment: HealthSys_RFI.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@healthsys.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-16T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial RFI - CPRA/service provider designation + dataflow questions

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, then attachments and a proposed next step:

1) Service provider designation: Redwood will accept SP/service provider treatment under CPRA/CPRA-like US state addenda for customer-controlled use cases. Suggested DPA language attached (see Redwood_SP_Onboarding_Playbook.pdf and later redline).

2) Telemetry: We categorize telemetry into three buckets: (a) per-request logs (latency, model id, token counts) retained 30 days; (b) aggregated performance metrics (no user identifiers) retained 24 months for product improvements; (c) debugging traces (may contain identifiers) retained up to 90 days and only accessible under our security incident or support workflows. None of this telemetry will be used for "sale" of personal information; we will include bounded-use language in the DPA.

3) Subprocessors: current list attached in the onboarding playbook. Notice window for non-critical subprocessor additions is 30 days via customer portal; for critical emergency onshore fallback (e.g., hardware outage) we may temporarily route to an approved onshore subprocessors pool and will notify within 48–72 hours and log the event in audit logs.

4) Transfer map: included (transfer-map.xlsx). High-level: production inference occurs in customer-chosen region when on Dedicated/Private; hosted mode routes to nearest region with fallback lanes noted. Transit vendors are listed in the playbook.

Next step: I'm attaching a short playbook and will follow with a proposed DPA redline (we can do a DocuSign flow). Would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday morning to run through the telemetry examples and subprocessor notice?

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_SP_Onboarding_Playbook.pdf (playbook stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-09-17T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial RFI - CPRA/service provider designation + dataflow questions

Aditya / Jonas —

Forwarding HealthSys RFI and my replies (see below). Quick operational asks before I send the redline DPA:

- Aditya: confirm SRE can back the 48–72 hour onshore fallback SLA for critical incidents (this is effectively an emergency route to onshore subprocessors). Do we have a defined list of onshore subprocessors that we can promise (and an attestation cadence)?

- Jonas: Legal asked for a short clause that states Redwood will not "sell" telemetry and will only use telemetry for service provision and product improvements. Can you review this suggested wording: "Provider shall use telemetry and usage logs solely to provide, maintain, and improve the Services; such telemetry shall not be sold or otherwise provided in exchange for monetary consideration or other valuable consideration to third parties." OK to include?

Notes: HealthSys also wants a 30-day notice for subprocessor additions (non-critical). We should accept that. They flagged evidence on transfer hops — I can include the transfer-map.xlsx.

Thanks — want to finalize the DPA redline by EOD Friday so I can get procurement review over the weekend.

Irene

Subject: Final - DPA redline and onboarding commitments (HealthSys pilot)

Elena / Carlos / Mike —

Thanks for the conversation earlier this week. Attached is our DPA redline (HealthSys_DPA_Redline_v2.docx) and the transfer map (transfer-map.xlsx). Summary of agreed points and binding commitments we will include in the DPA: 

- Service provider designation: Redwood accepts CPRA/US-state service provider treatment for the Services described in Schedule A. DPA includes explicit SP language and purpose limitation.
- Telemetry: three-tier classification confirmed (per-request logs: 30d; debugging traces: 90d; aggregated metrics: 24 months). Telemetry is used solely to provide and improve the Services and is not a "sale" under CPRA/CPRA-like statutes.
- Subprocessors: 30-day notice for non-critical additions via portal. For emergency onshore fallback we will temporarily route to an approved onshore subprocessors pool and notify within 48–72 hours; all such events will be captured in audit logs and post-incident report.
- Interstate transfers: transfer-map.xlsx enumerates transit hops and vendor partners; for Dedicated/Private deployments inference is region-controlled by customer.

Action items:
- Please review the attached redline and send any comments by end of day Wednesday so Procurement can sign off next week.
- If you would like this routed via DocuSign, here's a short link: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcdefg

If the above reads correctly I'll queue the DocuSign flow and include a short attestation appendix for onshore subprocessors. Thanks again — happy to hop on a follow-up if you need line-by-line review.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
